headlines.title: General Motors (GM) Puts 100% Recycled Battery Minerals Into Customer EVs
headlines.summary: General Motors (NYSE:GM) has rolled out EV batteries using cathode material made entirely from recycled nickel, cobalt, and manganese in a new pilot. The recycled minerals come from end-of-life GM EV battery packs processed by recycling partner Cirba Solutions. These 100% recycled critical minerals met original safety and performance specifications and are now installed in Cadillac Lyriq and Chevrolet Silverado EVs sold to customers.

headlines.title: GM CFO expects improved 2027 cash flow after EV restructuring
headlines.summary: As an “old school CFO,” a strong focus on cash flow and generation remains paramount, GM CFO Paul Jacobson said.

headlines.title: Ford Set To Lose Ground To Hyundai In Q3 Sales, Says Cox Automotive — ‘Detroit 3’ Market Share Seen Hitting Record Low

headlines.title: Who made this car? That's getting harder to answer

description: General Motors Company designs, builds, and sells trucks, crossovers, cars, and automobile parts worldwide. It operates through GM North America, GM International, and GM Financial segments. The company markets its vehicles primarily under the Buick, Cadillac, Chevrolet, GMC, Baojun, and Wuling brand names. In addition, it sells trucks, crossovers, cars, and automobile parts through retail dealers, distributors and dealers, as well as to fleet customers, including daily rental car companies, commercial fleet customers, leasing companies, and governments. Further, the company offers various range of after-sale services through dealer network, such as maintenance, light repairs, collision repairs, vehicle accessories, and extended service warranties. Additionally, it provides automotive financing; and software-enabled services and subscriptions. General Motors Company was founded in 1908 and is based in Detroit, Michigan.
